title: Orchestrator identity hardening: bound claims to machine/session evidence
outcome: The shared control plane records and validates richer worker identity (stable worker ID + machine + session token) so two workers cannot accidentally operate under the same identity, stale-lease recovery becomes faster and safer, and the lease/state-machine logic in orchestrator-core is protected by its own unit tests.
before: Mandate 2026-08-27 (Governor parallel-delivery directive, section 14): until authenticated worker identity is implemented, identity rests on convention; claim supports --machine but nothing validates uniqueness or binds a session to a claim. orchestrator-core.mjs lease/claim logic has no dedicated unit tests. The Governor has separately reduced lease_ttl_minutes from 90 to 30 in .viro/orchestrator.json in this activation commit.
after: Claims carry machine + a per-session token; a second live claim under the same worker ID with different session evidence is refused with a clear error; stale-assignment detection is unit-tested; identity fields appear in briefs and the team board.
acceptance: Backward compatible: existing state files without session tokens still load and operate; a state written by the old code is readable by the new code.
Duplicate live identity (same worker ID, different session token, unexpired heartbeat) is refused with an explicit error.
Unit tests cover claim/lease/stale/reap logic in orchestrator-core, runnable via node --test without the product app.
Both transports (REST and git) behave identically for the new identity fields.
Live dry-run against the real viro-agent-control branch proves claims, heartbeats, briefs and advances still work for an ordinary worker.
evidence: Unit test output for orchestrator-core lease logic
Backward-compatibility demo with a pre-change state file

builder.notes: Built by zcode-govtool-pc1 (worktree preserved through quota-wall reap) and completed by zcode-govtool-pc2 on pc-cloud1. Session-bound claims + duplicate-identity refusal in orchestrator-core (shared by both transports), additive state schema with a lazy adoption migration bridge, 23 unit tests for the lease/identity state machine runnable via node --test scripts/lib/, live duplicate-refusal and old-worker-compatibility dry-runs against the real viro-agent-control branch. Design contract in docs/agents/orchestrator-identity.md.

delta.before: Identity by convention; no core lease-logic unit tests.
delta.after: Session-bound identity with refusal on duplicate live identity, tested core logic, backward-compatible state.
proof: Unit tests 23/23 green via node --test scripts/lib/ (scripts/lib/orchestrator-core.test.mjs): scopesOverlap disjoint prefixes (tests/autosave-* vs tests/import-*), roleCanServe at every stage, depsSatisfied, 30-minute TTL staleAssignments, reapAssignment lease release, blockPacket, claim/lease lifecycle, duplicate-identity refusals, legacy-state and legacy-caller compatibility fixtures, identity in events/briefs/team board

Duplicate live identity refused live on the real viro-agent-control branch: re-claim of zcode-govtool-pc2/VIRO-0019 with a different session token while the heartbeat was unexpired exited 1 with 'duplicate live identity refused: worker 'zcode-govtool-pc2' already owns VIRO-0019 under session 'sess-vir…' from machine 'pc-cloud1'' and mutated no state

Live refusal also proven for wrong-session heartbeat ('identity conflict: ... the supplied session 'sess-imp…' does not match') and for throwaway agents zcode-0019-dryrun-a / zcode-0019-dryrun-b attempting to claim an assigned packet ('No conflict-free packet VIRO-0019 is claimable by builder')

Backward compatibility proven live: the pre-merge orchestrator (old code at main 72b05f0, primary repo) heartbeated the new-schema session-bound VIRO-0019 assignment without --session and all identity fields (assigned_session/assigned_machine/agents.session) survived the old-code write; new code also operated the real pre-change control state (claims/heartbeats/brief) throughout this session

Live ordinary-worker flow on the real control branch: claim (session mint/adopt), heartbeat with --session, idempotent resume of the original session, brief showing the identity block, state check 'Orchestration state is conflict-free.'
Both transports carry identical identity logic via orchestrator-core; REST script parses (node --check) but could not be live-tested without GITHUB_TOKEN; git transport proven live end-to-end
regression_protection: Ordinary claim/heartbeat/advance/reject flows unchanged and dry-run proven
scripts/lib/orchestrator-core.test.mjs pins legacy refusal messages and lease acquired_at preservation for pre-identity flows
Refusals throw IdentityConflictError before mutation, so rejected duplicates cannot corrupt shared state
delta.new_debt: sessions are disambiguation tokens, not auth credentials (documented in docs/agents/orchestrator-identity.md); scopesOverlap conservative prefix semantics pinned and recorded for a future Governor decision
